To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) VC style persistence is positively associated with VC performance; (ii) style persistence is higher for younger VC firms; (iii) style persistence is positively correlated with VC performance for young VC firms, but is negatively associated with performance for older VC firms; and (iv) VC style persistence and VC performance are negatively associated for VCs whose style persistence is correlated across time with the style persistence of other VC firms.
(1) style drift is detrimental to VC performance, (2) style persistence is beneficial to VC performance, and (3) economies of scale in style persistence are observed.
